newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: CRICKET-ENGLAND PARTNERSHIP TURNS TABLE ON NZ.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-ENGLAND PARTNERSHIP TURNS TABLE ON NZ.

text.p: England batsmen Alec Stewart and captain Mike Atherton dominated the morning session on the third day of the first cricket test against New Zealand at Eden Park on Sunday.
Resuming at 123 for one in reply to New Zealand's first innings 390, the pair batted through the session.
Stewart reached his 10th test century, and was on 104 at lunch while Atherton had fought his way to 79.
Stewart carried on where he left off on Saturday, striking the ball impressively and went to his hundred with a sharp single to mid on.
It came in 216 minutes, off 161 balls and included 14 fours and one six and was Stewart's fourth hundred against New Zealand.
By lunch the pair had put on 175 in 362 balls.
Stewart had a slice of luck shortly before lunch when umpire Steve Dunne rejected a desperately close appeal for leg before wicket off medium pacer Justin Vaughan.
Dunne initially began to raise his finger, then put his hand back behind his back.
Atherton, heading towards his 11th test century after a lean run on the tour of Zimbabwe and New Zealand, had batted almost four and a half hours, faced 208 balls and hit 10 boundaries.
